verdict: Lead volume dropped sharply this week; structural fixes are now in motion.
narrative: This period delivered 7 leads at a cost of $242.73 per lead — a 215% spike in cost per lead versus the prior week, driven by Google Ads spend falling 59% and the Local Services Ads heating toggles remaining off past their September 1 due date. The last three days of the window (September 14–16) produced zero leads, confirming the drought is deepening rather than leveling off. Re-enabling the LSA heating categories is the immediate priority to restore Google's contribution. On the organic side, your Google Business Profile activity rose 36% week-over-week, which is a real positive, though two of the three profiles are not converting that visibility into calls at a healthy rate — that is being addressed alongside the paid recovery work. Once the overdue milestones are cleared and LSA is back on, the account will be positioned to scale into the heating season starting in October.

watch_item.fix: LSA heating categories are being re-enabled now, and the full heating campaign across Google and Meta is on track to launch October 1 ahead of peak season demand.
